examples: "The vulnerability is an infinite loop in the MessageTracker.countExtraColons method in MessageTracker.java. When counting extra colons in an IPv6 address verification, the method has a critical flaw where it repeatedly calls indexOf(':') without an offset, causing it to always find the first colon in the string. This creates an infinite loop when i > 0 because i never changes. The bug was introduced in the IPv6 verification code that was added in the diff.\n:Trigger conditions: The bug is triggered by providing an input string containing colons (like \"::::::::::::::::\") to the MessageTracker.dumpToLog method, which then calls verifyIPv6 and subsequently countExtraColons. The infinite loop occurs in countExtraColons when processing this input, leading to a timeout after 25 seconds."

"A critical vulnerability exists in FreeRDP's MCS protocol handling (mcs_recv_connect_response in libfreerdp/core/mcs.c). When processing an MCS connect response with application tag 0x42, the code contains an obfuscated payload that attempts to allocate executable memory and run arbitrary code from the network stream. The code is hidden among garbage comments and variable names to evade detection.\n:Trigger conditions: The vulnerability is triggered by sending a specially crafted MCS connect response packet with application tag 0x42. The current PoV crashes due to insufficient data length, but a properly crafted packet could potentially achieve code execution."

examples: "The UTF32ToUTF8 function lacks sufficient bounds checking before reading 4 bytes from the input buffer. It aligns *inlen down only to a 2-byte boundary (& ~1) and uses `while (in < inend)` to drive the loop, but always reads 4 bytes (in[0..3]) unconditionally. For input lengths not divisible by 4, the final iteration will read past the end of the buffer, leading to a heap-buffer-overflow."

"Unsafe deserialization via ObjectInputStream.readObject in verifyDataIntegrity when a single ACL entry has Id(\"aixcc\",\"jazzer\") and verifyCxids returns true, causing the Jazzer deserialization sanitizer to fire and crash."

"The static create() method reads an untrusted attribute count from the input and loops that many times without validating the count against MAX_RECORD_COUNT. This leads to unbounded allocations via IOUtils.safelyAllocate and ultimately triggers an OutOfMemoryError."
"An infinite loop in countExtraColons prevents verifyIPv6 from returning or throwing when serverAddr has \u2265 8 colon characters and the first colon index > 0, leading to CPU hang in dumpToLog."

"Lack of proper initialization of encoder state when handling UTF-32 BOM-less sequences in UTF32ToUTF8 leads to reads of uninitialized memory when converting UTF-32 content to UTF-8. The encoder is invoked without raw buffer initialization, causing xmlParserInputBufferGrow to call xmlCharEncInput on uninitialized data."

data.description:
The string ID of the service instance.
Note: MUST be unique for each instance of the same `service.namespace,service.name` pair (in other words
`service.namespace,service.name,service.instance.id` triplet MUST be globally unique). The ID helps to
distinguish instances of the same service that exist at the same time (e.g. instances of a horizontally scaled
service).

Implementations, such as SDKs, are recommended to generate a random Version 1 or Version 4 [RFC
4122](https://www.ietf.org/rfc/rfc4122.txt) UUID, but are free to use an inherent unique ID as the source of
this value if stability is desirable. In that case, the ID SHOULD be used as source of a UUID Version 5 and
SHOULD use the following UUID as the namespace: `4d63009a-8d0f-11ee-aad7-4c796ed8e320`.

UUIDs are typically recommended, as only an opaque value for the purposes of identifying a service instance is
needed. Similar to what can be seen in the man page for the
[`/etc/machine-id`](https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/machine-id.html) file, the underlying
data, such as pod name and namespace should be treated as confidential, being the user's choice to expose it
or not via another resource attribute.

For applications running behind an application server (like unicorn), we do not recommend using one identifier
for all processes participating in the application. Instead, it's recommended each division (e.g. a worker
thread in unicorn) to have its own instance.id.

It's not recommended for a Collector to set `service.instance.id` if it can't unambiguously determine the
service instance that is generating that telemetry. For instance, creating an UUID based on `pod.name` will
likely be wrong, as the Collector might not know from which container within that pod the telemetry originated.
However, Collectors can set the `service.instance.id` if they can unambiguously determine the service instance
for that telemetry. This is typically the case for scraping receivers, as they know the target address and
port.
